judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit all five expectations with comparable specificity and citations; Report 1 additionally computes a rolling 12-month uptime figure while Report 2 adds a note that remediation should address the detection gap, but neither materially outperforms the other on the graded expectations.

report_1.evidence: failures began at 14:03 and the first alert fired at 14:50 — a **47-minute detection gap**, not "minutes."

report_2.evidence: checkout failures began at 14:03 and the first alert fired at 14:50 — a 47-minute detection gap.

report_1.evidence: The internal record, `larkpay-comms/incidents/OPS-412-timeline.md` (lines 9–10), states: "During the window 1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing; 37 were unrecoverable and refunded."

report_2.evidence: The internal timeline, `larkpay-comms/incidents/OPS-412-timeline.md` (lines 9–10), records that 1,284 transactions failed and required manual reprocessing, and 37 were unrecoverable and refunded.

report_1.evidence: `larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md` states the contractual monthly SLA is 99.9% and "any calendar month below 99.9% is a breach and owes service credits… (credits scale with the depth of the breach)." April 2026 was 99.77% (`larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv`, line 6) — a breach.

report_2.evidence: `larkpay-comms/metrics/uptime-2026.csv` (line 6) shows April 2026 at 99.77%, below the 99.9% contractual monthly SLA in `larkpay-comms/docs/sla-commitments.md`, which states that any month below 99.9% "is a breach and owes service credits."

report_1.evidence: This violates rule 1 of `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` ("Never assign blame to an individual").

report_2.evidence: `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` rule 1 says "Never assign blame to an individual."

report_1.evidence: Rule 3 of `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` requires leading with impact and remediation. The draft instead opens with a (false) uptime boast (lines 3–4), denies impact mid-document (line 10), and buries the sole remediation — "a pre-deploy validation step for configuration changes" — in the final line (line 21).

report_2.evidence: Rule 3 of `larkpay-comms/docs/customer-comms-style-guide.md` requires leading with impact and remediation, but the draft opens with an uptime boast (lines 3–4) and closes with marketing language about engineering culture (lines 16–19), burying impact (misstated) and remediation (single last line, line 21).
